data.name: Emulation.Help.Audio.Floppy.MuteEmpty.Detailed
data.value: Silences the emulated drive sound while no disk is inserted. Disable this option to keep the idle mechanical noise.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Audio.Filter.Detailed
data.value: Selects how the original analog audio filter is reproduced. Emulated follows the hardware behavior. The other choices force the filter on or off.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Audio.PolarizedFilter.Detailed
data.value: Applies the polarized filter to the generated audio signal. Enable it to reproduce the filtered sound. Disable it to keep the unfiltered signal.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Audio.Interpolation.Detailed
data.value: Selects how audio samples are calculated between generated sample points. Higher-quality methods produce smoother sound but require more processing.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Audio.Latency.Detailed
data.value: Sets the duration of the audio buffer. A shorter buffer reduces delay but can cause crackling. A longer buffer improves stability but increases delay.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Audio.PokeyStereo.Detailed
data.value: Adds a second emulated POKEY chip to produce stereo sound. Enable this option only for software that supports dual POKEY audio.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Audio.StereoSeparation.Detailed
data.value: Sets the separation between the left and right channels. A lower value mixes the channels together. A higher value keeps them farther apart.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Audio.Floppy.SoundType.Short
data.value: Select the floppy drive sound set

data.name: Emulation.Help.Audio.Floppy.SoundType.Detailed
data.value: Selects the sample set used for the mechanical sounds of emulated floppy drives. It does not change drive behavior or disk data.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Audio.FilterType.Detailed
data.value: Selects the hardware filter response to emulate. Auto follows the selected machine model. A specific choice always uses that filter response.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Controller.ParallelAdapter.Detailed
data.value: Emulates a parallel-port adapter that adds two joystick ports. Enable it for software that supports four simultaneous players.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Controller.TurboPulse.Detailed
data.value: Sets the time between automatic button presses produced by turbo. A shorter interval produces faster repeated firing.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Controller.Compatibility.Detailed
data.value: Selects a special controller mapping, such as dual-stick control, swapped ports, or Joy2B+. Choose None to keep the standard port mapping.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Controller.AnalogSensitivity.Detailed
data.value: Sets how strongly an analog input responds to movement. A higher value produces a larger response from the same physical movement.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Controller.DigitalSensitivity.Detailed
data.value: Sets how quickly a digital direction reaches full movement. A higher value makes direction changes reach their maximum more quickly.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Controller.Autofire.Detailed
data.value: Disabled turns autofire off. On button repeats fire while the assigned button is held. Always repeats fire continuously.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Controller.PaddleSpeed.Detailed
data.value: Sets how quickly digital input moves an emulated paddle. A lower value moves it more slowly. A higher value moves it more quickly.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Cpu.FpuModel.Detailed
data.value: Selects the floating-point unit used for floating-point instructions. Choose None to disable the FPU. Available models depend on the selected CPU.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Cpu.Precision.Detailed
data.value: Selects how closely CPU timing follows the original hardware. More accurate modes can improve compatibility but may require more processing.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Cpu.Speed.Detailed
data.value: Sets the processor frequency used by the emulated machine. The original speed preserves hardware timing. Higher values accelerate CPU-limited software.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Mouse.Analog.Short
data.value: Use analog sticks to control the mouse

data.name: Emulation.Help.Mouse.Analog.Detailed
data.value: Allows analog joystick axes to move the emulated mouse pointer. Enable it when a physical analog stick should control the pointer.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Mouse.AnalogSpeed.Detailed
data.value: Sets pointer speed when an analog stick controls the emulated mouse. A higher value moves the pointer farther for the same stick movement.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Mouse.AnalogDeadzone.Short
data.value: Set the analog mouse dead zone

data.name: Emulation.Help.Mouse.AnalogDeadzone.Detailed
data.value: Ignores small analog-stick movements around the center while controlling the mouse. Increase the value if the pointer moves while the stick is released.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Memory.AxlonShadow.Detailed
data.value: Mirrors the Axlon control bank at address $0F. Enable it only for software or memory expansions that use this additional address.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Memory.Axlon.Detailed
data.value: Sets the amount of bank-switched Axlon memory. Disabled removes the expansion. The other choices provide the selected memory capacity.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Memory.Mosaic.Detailed
data.value: Sets the amount of bank-switched Mosaic memory. Disabled removes the expansion. The other choices provide the selected memory capacity.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Memory.Extensions.Detailed
data.value: Sets the amount of additional expansion memory supported by the selected machine. Choose None to use only the configured main memory.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Memory.Fast.Detailed
data.value: Sets the amount of Fast RAM available directly to the CPU. Additional Fast RAM can help compatible software but changes the emulated hardware configuration.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Memory.MapRam.Detailed
data.value: Allows compatible software to map writable RAM into the system ROM address area. This option is available only on machine models that support MapRAM.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Memory.Z3.Detailed
data.value: Sets the amount of 32-bit Fast RAM connected through the Zorro III bus. Use it only with compatible 32-bit machines and software.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Memory.Slow.Detailed
data.value: Sets the amount of Slow RAM in the trapdoor expansion area. This memory is slower than Fast RAM and uses a different hardware address range.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Firmware.RomKey.Detailed
data.value: Selects the key file used to decrypt a licensed encrypted ROM image. Leave this field empty when the selected ROM is not encrypted.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Firmware.FastBoot.Detailed
data.value: Skips selected hardware initialization delays to shorten startup. Disable this option when software requires the original startup sequence.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Firmware.ExtendedRom.Detailed
data.value: Selects the secondary firmware ROM required by some machine models. Leave this field empty when the selected model does not use an extended ROM.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Storage.SioAcceleration.Detailed
data.value: Speeds up compatible transfers through the serial input/output bus. Disable this option when software depends on the original transfer timing.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Storage.CassetteBoot.Detailed
data.value: Makes the emulated machine try to start from the attached cassette image. Disable this option when starting from another device.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Storage.RealTimeClock.Detailed
data.value: Emulates an R-Time 8 real-time clock so compatible software can read the current date and time.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Storage.PrinterDevice.Detailed
data.value: Makes the emulated P: printer device available to software. Disable this option when printer-device emulation is not needed.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Storage.SerialDevice.Detailed
data.value: Makes the emulated R: serial device available to software. Disable this option when serial-device emulation is not needed.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Video.Artifacting.Detailed
data.value: Selects how high-resolution patterns produce composite-video colors. None disables artifact colors. The other modes reproduce different palettes or chip behavior.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Video.ImmediateBlits.Detailed
data.value: Selects whether blitter operations finish immediately or follow emulated hardware timing. Immediate mode is faster but less timing-accurate.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Video.HzChange.Detailed
data.value: Allows the output refresh rate to follow changes in the emulated video mode. Locked keeps the current output refresh rate.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Video.CollisionLevel.Detailed
data.value: Selects which sprite and playfield collisions are calculated. More complete detection improves compatibility but requires more processing.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Video.FlickerFixer.Detailed
data.value: Reduces flicker in interlaced video output. Enable it for a steadier image. Disable it to preserve the original interlaced display behavior.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Video.AspectRatio.Detailed
data.value: Selects how the emulated image is scaled horizontally and vertically. Auto follows the emulated output. A fixed choice forces that display shape.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Video.Gamma.Detailed
data.value: Changes the brightness of midtones without directly changing the black and white levels. Lower values darken midtones. Higher values brighten them.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Video.LineMode.Detailed
data.value: Selects how vertical video lines are displayed. Auto follows the emulated mode. Other choices force single lines, doubled lines, or scanlines when available.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Video.Standard.Detailed
data.value: Selects the emulated television timing, such as PAL or NTSC. This affects refresh rate, hardware timing, and software compatibility.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Video.ExternalPalette.Detailed
data.value: Selects a predefined color palette instead of colors generated from the current video settings. Choose None to use the generated colors.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Video.Colors.Detailed
data.value: Selects the color depth used to render the image. 24-bit keeps more color detail. 16-bit uses a smaller range of colors.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Video.Region.Detailed
data.value: Selects the regional timing used by the emulated machine. The choice can affect video frequency, CPU timing, and compatible firmware.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Video.Rendering.Detailed
data.value: Selects the graphics backend used to draw the emulated display. Available renderers can differ in performance and compatibility with the host system.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Video.ColorDelay.Detailed
data.value: Sets the GTIA color phase delay used to reproduce colors. Default uses the standard value. Numeric choices shift the resulting hues.

data.name: Emulation.Help.Video.FrameSkip.Detailed
data.value: Sets how many display frames are omitted. Disabled draws every frame. Higher values reduce rendering work but make motion less smooth.
